en: Oṃ, salutation to Prajāpati. Oṃ, salutation to Pṛthivī. Oṃ, salutation to Pururāja. Oṃ, salutation to Agni. Oṃ, salutation to Śrī. Having offered the food offering (naivedya): Oṃ jū saḥ, may there be the supreme attainment of food. Oṃ aṃttaśca. In all transformations, you are the one who dwells in the secret cave, the foremost in every way; you are the state of Brahman, you are the state of Viṣṇu.

Rudratva, svāhā! You are the *vaṣaṭ* call; you are the beginningless one, the light, the essence, the immortal—svāhā! Om, svāhā to Prāṇa; Om, svāhā to Apāna; Om, svāhā to Samāna; Om, svāhā to Udāna; svāhā to Vyāna. This is the *pañcagrāma*. Om, having drunk water as the "spreading of immortality" (*amṛtopastaraṇa*). Om.
One who is devoted to the nectar of immortality should destroy the darkness of water that has reached the crest of the head.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O Vajreśvarī, who has entered the center of the diamond-pavilion, Hrīṃ Krīṃ Aiṃ! Aiṃ Krīṃ! Salutation to the eternal passion, the diamond-dust Nityā!
Hrīṃ! O Bhuvaneśvarī, honor my banner; svāhā!
For washing the face: a tilaka made with yellow orpiment, lodhra, vippalī, manaḥśilā, and combined with horse saliva,
is all-enchanting.
Oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ blīṃ saḥ! O Blessed One, at the birth of the grandson, protect me along with all my people; svāhā!
With unbroken grains, having performed the recitation and applied the *tilaka*: *Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ*, I worship the feet of Vāgeśvarī.

*Oṃ hreṃ śroṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, you who bear a mass of tawny matted hair, O radiant one with a flaming mouth, three-eyed one, accept this offering (*bali*)! Svāhā! (Twice). *Oṃ hāṃ*, [to the principle of] Vidya-tattva, svāhā! *Oṃ*.

HŪṂ ŚIVATATTVĀYA SVĀHĀ || OṂ HAḤ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ | OṂ ASTRĀYAYA PHAṬ (6) OṂ HĀṂ HRDAYĀYA NAMAḤ | OṂ HRĪṂ ŚIRASE SVĀHĀ || OṂ HŪṂ ŚIKHĀYAI VAṢAṬ | OṂ HAṂ KAVACĀYA HUṂ | OṂ HAUṂ NETRATRAYĀYA VOṢAṬ | OṂ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ || KARANYĀSAḤ | AṄGANYĀSAḤ ||
Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ [insert mantra] oṃ heṃ kavacāya oṃ | Avaguṇṭha.
Oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ—protection. Oṃ hauṃ śaktaye vauṣaṭ. [Form] the dhenumudrā. Oṃ hoṃ śivāya vauṣaṭ. Hāṃ hṛdayāya vauṣaṭ. Oṃ huṃ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ. Heṃ kavacāya vauṣaṭ. Oṃ haḥ astrāya vauṣaṭ.

Oṃ heṃ kavacāya hūṃ. To the one who dwells upon Mount Laṅkā. Oṃ sa (12) recaka, haṃ (12) pūraka (12), oṃ yaṃ (12) kumbhaka; recaka, pūraka, kumbhaka. Oṃ raṃ (12) recaka, pūraka, kumbhakaḥ. Oṃ vaṃ (16). O you who wear red garments, O you with red matted hair, O you who are the knower of the path, O young maiden seated upon a lotus throne, laugh!

One should meditate upon Brahmāṇī, the eighteenth [deity], seated on a lotus, possessing four faces and four arms, adorned with a garland of *śrṛṅgī* flowers; she holds a water-pot (*tuṇḍa*) in her right hand and a *kamaṇḍalu* in her left, and is seated upon a red lotus. [This is] the meditation (*dhyāna*).

Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the heart; taking water in the left hand (3). Oṃ hā hī hṛṃ hoṃ hoṃ haḥ—[one should] with effort [recite this] over that very water. Oṃ heṃ, salutation to the armor, hūṃ; protect, O best of heroes! Oṃ haḥ, salutation to the weapon, phaṭ; may it be protected. Oṃ hāṃ hoṃ, salutation to Śiva, vauṣaṭ. Oṃ hraṃ, salutation to the heart, vauṣaṭ. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the head, vauṣaṭ.

Khāyai vauṣaṭ | Oṃ Heṃ kavacāya vauṣaṭ | Oṃ Hraḥ astrāya vauṣaṭ | One should consecrate oneself. [With] the remainder of the water... [for] the herb... for the protection of the void... One should recite the Gāyatrī mantra three times with the root mantra: Oṃ tanmaheśāya vidmahe vāgviśuddhāya dhīmahe tanno śivaḥ.
May it impel [me]. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the heart. Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the [head]. Oṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the crest-lock (śikhā).
Oṃ heṃ, svāhā to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ hoṃ, svāhā to the three eyes. Oṃ haḥ, svāhā to the weapon (astra). Oṃ, svāhā to the Ādityas. Oṃ, svāhā to the Vasus. Oṃ, svāhā to the Bhṛgus.
Oṃ, svāhā to the Viśvedevas! Oṃ, svāhā to the Mādhyas! Oṃ, svāhā to the Maruts! Oṃ, svāhā to the Bhṛgus! Oṃ, svāhā to the Aṅgirasas! O hosts of gods, this is the divine tirtha of austerity.
Seated upon a seat together with the host of the Jyotirgaṇa: *Oṃ* to Atri, Svāhā! To Vasiṣṭha, Svāhā! To Pulastya, Svāhā! To Bhṛgu, Svāhā!
To Bharadvāja, Svāhā! To Viśvāmitra, Svāhā! To Pracetas, Svāhā! These...
The finger-joints: Oṃ, svāhā to Sanaka; Oṃ, svāhā to Śunanda; [Oṃ, svāhā] to Nātanā;
svāhā to Kapila; svāhā to Cāsu; Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to Coḍha; vaṣaṭ to Pañcaśikha. [To] Dhvajamānava; [to] Bhīma; to the seven men; to all beings, to all beings, voṣaṭ!

Vauṣaṭ to all the piśācas! Vauṣaṭ to all the rākṣasas! Vauṣaṭ to all the nāgas! [This is] from the root of the hand in gambling. In this [rite] for the sake of the owl (ulūka), with water mixed with kuśa grass and sesame seeds: Oṃ, svāhā to Kavyarāla! Oṃ, svadhā to Soma! Oṃ, svadhā to Yama!
To Anyamāna, svadhā! Oṃ, to Agniṣṭha, svāhā! Oṃ, to Vahiṣaṣṭhya, svadhā! Oṃ, to Ājñaya, svadhā!
O gods and ancestors, satisfy yourselves with ghee! Oṃ, to the fathers, svadhā! Oṃ, to the grandfathers, svadhā!
Oṃ, to the great-grandfathers, svadhā! Oṃ, to the mothers, svadhā! Oṃ...

Oṃ, svadhā to the maternal grandfathers. Oṃ, svadhā to the maternal great-grandfathers. Oṃ, svadhā to the maternal great-great-grandfathers. Svadhā to all paternal ancestors. Svadhā to all maternal ancestors. Svadhā to all [lineages] of every *gotra*. Oṃ, svadhā to the principle of the Self (*ātmatattva*). Oṃ.

Hrīṃ, svadhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva). Oṃ hūṃ, svadhā to the principle of Śiva (śiva-tattva). Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana): Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saṃ, obeisance to Sūrya. Oṃ glūṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to Śiva. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vauṣaṭ to Mṛtyujaya. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vauṣaṭ to Amṛta-ma[heśvara]. Oṃ juṃ saḥ...
Salutation to Amṛtīśvarabhairava. Oṃ aghore hāṃ, thaghore, ghoratara heṃ, sarvataḥ sarva sarve heṃ ho juṃ saḥ, namaste rudrarūpe hraḥ hūṃ, salutation to the pure Mahābhairava.

Oṃ hrīṃ aghoreśvarī hūṃ phaṭ || Oṃ hrauṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Caṇḍī Kātyāyanī, the Great Durgā. This is the root mantra (mūlamantra). We know that Great Lord; we meditate upon Him whose speech is pure; may He, Śiva, impel us. This is the Gāyatrī.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, with a mass of tawny matted hair, O Jvālāmukha, three-eyed one, accept this offering and worship! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Vaṭu!
Oṃ Juṃ Saḥ! To all spirits, from the various forms beginning with Vyākaraṇa up to Vibhūti, who reside in the netherworld (pātāla).

May those who are present be satisfied by this *balikarman*. Bhūta! Oṃ gāṃ gīṃ guṃ geṃ goṃ gaḥ, Gaṇapati, accept this *bali*, svāhā! Oṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣeṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ, Kṣetrapāla of your own abode, accept this *bali*, svāhā! Oṃ aiṃ, I worship the sandals of the venerable Guru. Hlīṃ.
*Astrāya phaṭ* | *Klīṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Hlīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*. *Hklīṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vauṣaṭ*.
*Hklīṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *hūṃ*. *Hklīṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*.
Meditative absorption.
One should meditate on [the deity] who is red in color, wearing a crown of matted hair with the crescent moon as its crest-ornament;
four-armed, holding a single vajra, a noose, and a goad in the left hands, and [the remaining implements] in the right;
seated upon a red lotus. HKLĪM. I worship the venerable sandals of Vāmeśvarī. Thus.
[The deity] shines in the vessel. O mind, offer the bali-oblation with this mantra, along with incense, lamps, and food offerings. Homage!
Here, with this mantra (* * *?), perform the sprinkling (tarpaṇa) and the dissolution (saṃhāra) into the heart. Oṃ namaḥ śivāya.
Perform the assignment of the hands (kara-nyāsa) and the assignment of the limbs (aṅga-nyāsa). For the worship of the two [deities], [recite]: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Śivāśna; Oṃ hāṃ haṃ.

(*? Salutation to the form of Śiva. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the deity of knowledge (Vidyādeva). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the heart; oṃ hīṃ, svāhā to the head; oṃ hūṃ, salutation to the crest-lock (śikhā); oṃ haṃ, salutation to the armor (kavaca); oṃ (* *?), phaṭ to the weapon (astra). The ritual worship (pūjāścana): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the heart. Laṃ [khva]kāyārodraṃ svaṃśai(?).

Enveloping with the armor (*kavaca*): the protection against weapons. *Oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ*. I worship the vessel of offering (*arghapātra*). *Oṃ hāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*. With this mantra, [one performs] the sprinkling (*laṃṣvathaṃ*). *Oṃ*. Recitation (*jāpa*) of the vessel of offering. Bathing of the deity. Worship of the Sun. Worship of Viṣṇu. Ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Worship of the door. *Oṃ hāṃ*.

Salutation to Gaṇapati: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śaravatī. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī—in the center. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Nandin; Oṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati—in the south. [In the] north: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Mahākāla; Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Yamunā. Haḥ, to the weapon, phaṭ. [This is for] the bathing jar: Oṃ haḥ, to the weapon, phaṭ.

At the door, one bathes: *Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the Lord of Speech.* At the southern door: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati*; he is seated upon the pedestal of Gaṇapati. *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Gurus*; they are seated upon the pedestal of the Gurus. *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ādhāraśakti*; this is the seat of the Self. Having performed *prāṇāyāma*, [one performs] the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
Worship of the Argha Vessel. The Mantra for the Water Vessel: Sandalwood, unbroken rice grains. *Oṃ haravāya namaḥ*.

Encircle with the Armor (Kavaca) mantra. The Great Mudrā (Mahāmudrā). Worship of oneself. [With] that same [mantra], having seen [the offerings], [worship] with sandalwood and unbroken rice grains: *Oṃ hāṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ*, *Oṃ gurubhyo namaḥ*, *Oṃ hāṃ*.

Salutation to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Seat of Ananta (Anantāsana). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Dharma. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Jñāna. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vairājña. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Īśvarya.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Adharma. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ajñāna. Oṃ, salutation to Avairājña. Oṃ hāṃ...
Oṃ, homage to Anaiśvarya; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Adhaścchanda; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Ūrdhvacchāda.
The Root Seat (Mūlasthāna): Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Padmāsana; Hāṃ, homage to Padma; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Karṇikā;
Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Vāmā; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Jyeṣṭhā; Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Raudrī; Oṃ...

Hāṃ, obeisance to Kālī; hāṃ, obeisance to Kalavikarṇī. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Balapramathanī; oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sarvakṛtadayānī; oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Manonmanī. [The eight offerings. Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to Sūryamaṇḍalā; hāṃ, obeisance to Somamaṇḍalā.
Oṃ, homage to the fire mandala; Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the seat of Śiva.
Meditative concentration (dhyāna).
Oṃ. There, the Lord sits upon a lion-throne resembling pure crystal;
he has five faces, ten mighty arms, and three eyes on each face.
Richly adorned with the splendor of matted locks and a crown, with the crescent moon shimmering as his crest-ornament,
his lotus-like hands are gracefully occupied with a spear, a trident, and a six-pronged vajra.
Furthermore, with his five hands, he holds a hand-drum (ḍamaru) in the right, a citron (bījapūra) in the left, and a snake, a rosary, and blue lotuses.
One should install Sadāśiva, endowed with the thirty-two marks, seated upon a bound lotus throne; this is the Śaiva form whose sphere of perception extends to the end of Śakti.
*Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Form of Śiva.* [Performing] the rites beginning with invocation until the conclusion, [one says]: "Obeisance to Śiva."

Water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamana*). Sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), flowers, incense, lamp, and food offering (*naivedya*): *Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ*, obeisance to the Form of Śiva (*śivamūrti*). *Oṃ Haṃ*, obeisance to the Body of Brahmā (*vidhādeha*). *Oṃ Hāṃ Hauṃ*, obeisance to Śiva. *Oṃ Hāṃ*, obeisance to the Heart. [This is] the worship of the Heart and other limbs (*hṛdayādi-pūjā*). With the root mantra, perform the triple *añjali* gesture three times.

Having performed the five-fold offerings (*pañcopacāra*) with the root mantra, one should ring the bell and other musical instruments. [One performs] the lineage (*gotra*), the dissolution [of obstructions] with the mudrā, and [the invocation]: *oṃ ādhāraśakti-kamalāsanāya namaḥ*. [Then follows] the seat for the self (*ātmāsana*) and breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). *aiṃ hklīṃ astrāya phaṭ*; *aiṃ hklīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *aiṃ hklīṃ śirase*.
*svāhāḥ aiṁ ha hklīṁ śikhāyai voṣaṭ | aiṁ kklīṁ kavacāya hūṃḥ aiṁ klīṁ netratrayāya voṣaṭ aiṁ hklīṁ astrāya phaṭ |* Having performed the *kara-nyāsa* and *aṅga-nyāsa*,
one should establish the *arghapātra* (offering vessel). *hasakṣamalavarayūṁ saḥ saḥ ānandabhairavāya vaṣaṭ |*

Glūṃ mlūṃ plūṃ slūṃ nlūṃ: worship with the root mantra for the heart and other limbs, and for the *arghapātra*. With the mantra "Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, I worship the sandals of Kāmeśvarī," one should worship one's own head. Then, having worshipped the *cakra*:
"Obeisance to the seat of Kāmeśvarī; obeisance to the form of Kāmeśvarī. One should meditate [upon her].
Red in color, with a crown of matted hair adorned by the crescent moon, four-armed and one-faced,
holding a noose and a goad in her left hands and a conch-shell and a rosary in her right hands, she sits upon a red lotus seat.

The invocation and installation [are performed]; the worship of the heart and other limbs is done with the root mantra, using sandalwood, unbroken rice, and flowers. *Aiṃ naṃ*, I worship the sandals of Nandā in the east.
Aiṃ Saṃ, I worship the sandals of Śubhagā. Aiṃ, I worship the sandals of Śiraḥraktā. Aiṃ Raṃ, I worship the sandals of Rati.
Aiṁ Paṁ, I worship the sandals of Prīti. Aiṁ Maṁ, I worship the sandals of Manobhavā.
[I offer] incense, lamp, food offering, flowers, betel, libations, and so forth with the root mantra. Having given the *bali* offering:
Recitation of mantras, hymns of praise, prostrations, and dismissal with the appropriate mudrā. [Thus ends the auspicious chapter on the ritual procedure for the worship of Kāmeśvarī.]

Oṃ, salutations to the glorious gurus. Having risen during the *brāhma-muhūrta*, having prostrated at the feet of the guru, and having performed purification (*śauca*), sipping of water (*ācamana*), and rinsing of the mouth, one should invoke the sacred ford (*tīrtha*) with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, purify it with the *vāgbhava* mantra, immerse oneself in the water, and recite the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).

Having requested seven handfuls of grain with the *kāla-mudrā*, having put on his lower garment, and having meditated upon the form of the Sun with the tips of his fingers in the water, he should cast [the grain] onto the *vajra-śilā* while reciting the mantra. Then, he should moisten it with water held in his left hand that has been consecrated seven times with the mantra: *oṃ kṣāṃ saḥ mārtaṇḍabhairavāya*.

Salutation to the one endowed with the power of illumination (*prakāśa-śakti*). Having gratified the Guru with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), one should offer libations (*tarpaṇa*) to the Devas, Ṛṣis, Pitṛs, Bhūtas, Bhairavas, Yoginīs, and Kṣetrapālas: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ādityebhyaḥ svāhā* (3);
*oṃ rudrebhyaḥ svāhā* (3); *vasubhyaḥ svāhā* (3); *aṅgirobhyaḥ svāhā* (3); *mātṛbhyaḥ*...
Whether one is in a state of prosperity or a pauper, an outcaste or born of a twice-born lineage—there is no distinction of caste in the worship of the Linga; Rudra is equally present in all.
Born into the lineage of Śiva, he was free from the cycle of birth through the practice of Dharma;
Umā was his mother, Rudra his father, and the Lord (Īśvara) was his very family.

For those whose mother is Pārvatī and whose father is Īśa, the Great Lord, what distinction of caste or family can there be for them? For them, the firm conviction that Śiva is the goal is itself their initiation.
When one's mind is dissolved in Śiva, you should consider that person as superior even to the gods;
whereas for one who perceives the Śivaliṅga as a mere stone, it is like a sin.
The Śūdra-hood of the Śūdra has passed away, and the twice-born status of the Brāhmaṇa likewise; when one is perfected through immersion in the essence of Śiva, distinctions of caste no longer exist.
On the tips of the big toes are sixty-eight sacred fords (*tīrtha*); on the two feet are the seven oceans;
on the two hands are Daṇḍākṣī and Amūrttāniga; and on the shanks are the mobile [sacred sites].
Svāhā (3). Māyāyai svāhā (3). Bhadrakālyai svāhā (3). Agastyāya svāhā (3).
Subhaṃkaryai svāhā. Kaḍhātre svāhā (3). Vāgīśvaryai svāhā (3). To Atri, Vasiṣṭha, and the other sages.

Svāhā (3). To Kavyavāhana and the others, Svāhā (3). To the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, Svāhā (3). Oṃ, we know Tripura; we know Kāmeśvarī; may that Kṛiṃ impel us. Then, having drawn a mandala with vermilion paste and other substances, [one offers] to the essence of the nature of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra.
Salutation to the Pīṭha. Having visualized the wheel, having worshipped the planets beginning with the Moon,
having worshipped the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Aries, having worshipped the twenty-seven lunar mansions beginning with Aśvinī,
[one should offer] salutation to the fifteen lunar days beginning with the first (pratipad), and salutation to the yogas beginning with Viṣkambha.

Having filled a copper vessel with red sandalwood, *karavīra* flowers, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), and *dūrvā* grass along with *śallakī*, one should offer the *argha* water while reciting the root mantra one hundred and eight times.
Then follows the worship of the door: "Gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati; Vāṃ, obeisance to Vaṭukabhairava; Duṃ..."

*Durgāyai namaḥ; kṣāṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ. On the threshold (dahalyā), on the right and left [hands]: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kāmadeva-ratye namaḥ; vasantāya prītyai namaḥ; gāṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ; sāṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ; cāṃ śriyai namaḥ; oṃ dehalyai namaḥ. Then, [offer] unbroken rice (akṣata).*

Having offered *kuśa* grass and water for the *nārāca-āstra*, [one recites]: "May those beings who have departed from here, those established upon the earth, and those beings who create obstacles—may they depart with auspicious intent. *Oṃ hrai astrāya phaṭ*.
Then, one flower for the mandala; thereafter, the seat: "Salutations to Kālāgnirudra."
Salutation to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti); salutation to Ananta; salutation to Kurma; salutation to Pṛthivī; salutation to the Altar (Vedikā).
Then, from the east (Indra’s direction) and so forth, [offer] to the ten [directions]:
Oṃ, salutation to Ādhāraśakti. Having performed the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) upon the broad seat (āsana), [one should proceed].

Having described the triangle, the eight-cornered [figure], the twenty-cornered, the fourteen-cornered, the nine-cornered, the eight-petalled, the sixteen-petalled, and the four-gated square with vermilion and other substances—
[one should worship] "Salutation to the sandals of the entire circle of the secret and manifest Yoginīs. Having formed the *trikhaṇḍa* mudrā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, O Tripuraśundarī, obeisance to the one seated upon the ocean of nectar—at the feet (3).

O Tripuraśundarī, obeisance to the one seated upon the lotus-feet—at the knees (3). Obeisance to the one whose self is food for the Goddess Tripuraśundarī—at the thighs. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ, O Tripuravāsinī, obeisance to the one seated upon the moon—at the hips.

*Namaḥ*. At the buttocks: *Tripurā Devī*, *namaḥ* to the seat of all the Mothers. At the anus: *Hrīṃ Klīṃ Ddeṃḥ Tripuramālinī*, *namaḥ* to the seat of the accomplishment of the goal. One should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the Mother of the Mātṛkās beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha.
Then: *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Āṃ*, [to] Vasinī, the Goddess of Speech.

Homage! (3) *Riṃ Klhrīṃ*, homage to Kāmeśvarī, the goddess of speech. (3) *Oṃ Rīṃ Myvlīṃ*, homage to Modinī, the goddess of speech. (3) *Oṃ Ymlūṃ*, homage to Vimalā, the goddess of speech. (3) *Smḷvyuṃ*, homage to Aruṇā, the goddess of speech. (3) *Paṃ Jmvyuṃ*, homage to Jamini, the goddess of speech. Yaḥ.

*Smvdyuṃ*, obeisance to the Goddess of Speech, the Sovereign of All. (3) *Śaṃ śmvlyuṃ*, obeisance to the Goddess of Speech, Kaulinī. (3) One should enter through the Brahma-aperture, the forehead, the space between the eyebrows, the throat, the heart, the navel, the secret place, the feet, and the hips by means of the Root-Vidyā. [In the abode of desire, she who is] the Goddess Kāmeśvarī...

I worship the venerable sandals (śrīpādukā) of the power (śakti) whose self is Rudra. Having uttered the seed-syllable (bīja) in the center of the arrow within the triangle of the support (ādhāra) and the eight corners, in the solar wheel (sūryacakra) at the sacred seat (pīṭha) of Jālandhara, I worship the venerable sandals of the goddess Vajreśvarī, whose power is Viṣṇu. In the right corner, having uttered the third seed-syllable, [I worship] in the cavern of Pūrṇagiri.

I worship the Śrī-pādukā of the Goddess Mālinī, the power whose essence is Rudra. In its left corner, having recited the root-vidyā, I worship the Śrī-pādukā of the Goddess Mahātripurasundarī at the Brahma-cakra in the seat of Oḍḍiyāna, the power whose essence is the Supreme Brahman. In the center of that is the Ādhāra-hṛdaya.

One should worship the three principles of the Self (ātmatattva) within the apertures of Brahmā (brahmarandhra). [One should perform] the Ṣaḍā-mudrā, the Triśūla-mudrā, the Yoni-mudrā, and the Padmāsana. Having visualized a triangle within the vessel for the guest-offering (arghapātra), one should contemplate the Khaḍgāsanas in its center;
then, in the right and left corners in front of it, the three goddesses beginning with Kāmā, and below them, the other deity.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the *kṣa*-mantra on the head and likewise purified the three triangles, one should meditate upon Kuṇḍalinī and begin the external worship. Then, at the door of the sacrificial pavilion (*jāgamaṇḍapa*), one should worship Gaṇapati and Kṣetrapāla on the right and left [respectively].
Within the sixteen-petaled lotus, one should worship the lineage of gurus beginning with Śrī Śiva, and then [the deities] in the southeast.

In the spaces between the petals [are] Maitrīsa, Uḍīsa, and the sixty Carccā Nāthas. Starting from the western door as the seventh, upon the sixfold seat beginning with the square in the maṇḍala, one should utter the three-peaked seed-syllable of Bālā and then "Mahātripurasundarī, obeisance. Thereafter follows the meditation.

Having meditated with this [mantra] and uttered the three seed-syllables: "O Tripurasundarī, whose form is the bliss of oneness within the forest of great lotuses; O Mother, who acts for the welfare of all beings, come, come, O Supreme Goddess!"

Then, having displayed the mudrās beginning with the invocation: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, I worship the sandals of the supernatural powers (*siddhis*) beginning with *aṇimā*. (3) The power of levity (*laghimā-siddhi*). (3) The power of lordship (*īśitva-siddhi*). (3) The power of subjugation (*vasitva-siddhi*). (3) The power of irresistible will (*prākāmya-siddhi*). (3) The power of enjoyment (*bhukti-siddhi*). (3) The power of fulfillment of desires (*icchā-siddhi*). (3) The power of mastery (*vasitva-siddhi*). (3) The power of liberation (*mokṣa-siddhi*). Then, *Oṃ Brahmāṇy-ādi*...
I worship the sandals. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the Saṃkṣobhaṇī mudrā.
(3) Sarvavidrāviṇī (3) Sarvākarkhaṇī (3) Sarvvaveṣadhāriṇī (3) Sarvvomādiṇī (3) Sarvvamahāṅkuśā (3) Sarvvaviśveśvarī (3). Trikhaṇḍā is the Yoni-mudrā of the lotus.
On the sixteen petals: I worship the Śrī-pādukā of Ākarkhaṇī Nityā-kalā Kārmaṇī Nityā.

The one who churns the intellect, the one who churns the ego, the one who churns sound, the one who churns touch, the one who churns form, the one who churns taste, the one who churns smell, the one who churns dissolution, the one who churns duality,
the one who churns non-duality, the one who churns the mind, the one who churns the individual soul, the one who churns the Self, the one who churns nectar.

One should worship the body-encircling [deities] in the sequence of the eastern egg: "I worship the venerable sandals of the goddess Śrī Tripurasundarī, the young maiden (Bālā). On the eight petals: "I worship the venerable sandals of the goddess Anaṅgakusumā; [2] Anaṅgamekhalā; [3] Anaṅgamadanā."

Anaṅgamadanāturā (4), Anaṅgarekhā (5), Anaṅgāṅkuśā (6), Anaṅgamālinī (7), and the goddess Tripurasundarī—(8) I worship the Śrīpādukā. [These are to be worshipped in counter-clockwise order on the fourteen-spoked wheel. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the goddess Śrīpādukā of the power Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇī (3).

(3) She who causes all to flee; (3) she who causes all to tremble; (3) she who causes all to rejoice; (3) she who causes all to be deluded; (3) she who causes all to be paralyzed; (3) she who effects the entry [of all]; (3) she who causes all to be colored; (3) she who causes all to be intoxicated; (3) she who accomplishes all aims; (3) she who fulfills all prosperity; (3) she who fulfills all hopes.

I worship the sandals of the Goddess who dwells in Śrīripura, who consists of all mantras and who strikes fear into all dualities. (3) In the center, I worship the sandals of the one who bestows all accomplishments. (3)

Bestower of prosperity (3), maker of all dear (3), performer of all auspiciousness (3), bestower of all desires (3), liberator from all suffering (3), pacifier of all death (3), remover of all obstacles (3),
beautiful in every limb (3), [bestower of] all good fortune (3)— O Śrī Tripurā, [I worship] your sandals.

I worship (3). In the center is the triangle; from the west to the east, in the south is the weapon-enclosure (*?). Aiṁ drāṁ drīṁ klīṁ blūṁ saḥ aiṁ yāṁ rāṁ lāṁ vāṁ sāṁ, obeisance to the Jambhana [arrows] of Kāmeśvara, the arrows of desire. To the bow of Mohana, the Lord of Desire.

Salutations (3) to the bow of Mohanā Kāmeśvarī; salutations (3) to the bow of Vasīkaraṇā; salutations (3) to the goad of Staṃbhanā Kāmī; salutations (3) to the goad of Janman of Kāmeśvarī; Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ, I worship the sandals of the Goddess whose essence is Śrī Tripura (3). Having offered a handful of flowers.
One should offer Kāmeśvarī and the others in the corners of the triangle, and Tripurasundarī in the center;
thus, having worshipped them, one should present flowers, incense, perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings (*naivedya*).
One should place the offering vessels (*balipātra*) upon the pillars situated in the south, north, east, and west directions. Vāṃ.

Salutation to Vaṭukanātha. Jāṃ, svāhā to the Yoginīs. Kṣāṃ, salutation to Kṣetrapāla. Gāṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati. (3) Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ | Va | Hrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ Yo | Aiṃ Klīṃ Hsroṃḥ Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ Kṣeṃ Kṣoṃ Kṣaḥ Hūṃ, O Kṣetrapāla! Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Glauṃ Gāṃ, O Gaṇapati!

Thus ends the Bali-mantra. Having unified the inner theft (*antasteya*) and the outer theft (*vahisteya*), and having circumambulated three times the Goddess who is dark-hued, one offers the lamp-oblation (*dīpa-nivedana*) with that [mantra]: "O Goddess, Sovereign of the entire Cakra, whose nature is the Root-Goddess, accept this *ārārttika* for my success. Then, with the Root-Vidyā, [one offers] to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī many various...
Accept the food offering, svāhā! Having recited the mantra according to one's capacity:
"O Secret One, secret from the secret, protect us; what has been done and what has been recited [is offered]."
When [the deity] has been re-established through your grace by means of the *bhūta-maya* [mantra],

having offered [the ritual items] with another [mantra], having displayed the ten mudrās, having recited the hymn [asking] "Why?", having prostrated, and having presented the bell and other musical instruments, one should dissolve oneself, the Supreme Goddess, the retinue, and the sacrificial offering (*bali*) with the syllable *cuhuku*.
Having asked for forgiveness with the *samaya-vidyā* of the goddesses beginning with Kāmeśvarī, and having offered a handful of flowers once;

having presented the threefold offering of flowers and so forth; and having smelled with the nostrils through the *brahmaraṃdhra* the form of light consisting of the essence of the *tatatā* [the pervasive state], which resides within the maṇḍala, by means of the *kusumaṇa-saṃsarpa-mudrā*.

Having disciplined himself and attained the state of supreme Śiva-sāmarasya (union with the Supreme Śiva), having drawn [the vital energy] up through the path of the Suṣumṇā from the Mūlādhāra, and being liberated while living (jīvanmukta) according to the prescribed rite, he should partake of the *prasāda* and *caru* at the feet of the venerable Lord (Śrīnātha). With his mind dissolved in Him, he should dwell in bliss. [Thus ends [the section concerning] the venerable Goddess Mahātripurasundarī.]
[The manual is completed.]
Oṃ, homage to Gaṇapati! Hasa-kara-la-oṃ. Kara-la-hrīṃ. Sa-kala-harī. Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ glūṃ gāṃ:
to Gaṇapati, the bestower of boons, bring all people here, svāhā! Four-armed one, adorned with the crescent moon, with breasts bowed down, red as the hue of saffron, [holding] noose and goad...
Obeisance to you, O sole Mother of the universe, who holds a flower in your hand. Ka e oṃ laharī oṃ rīṃ sklhrīṁḥ.
Who is she?
She whose jeweled casket is upon her lips; how is she, the beloved, so delightful? This is the secret instruction of the Guru.
With breasts bowed by the weight of youth, her form is most excellent, fragrant with the arrows of love, and sweet as honey.
One should offer with the left hand at night that which is most delightful and inexhaustible. Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ oṃ namaḥ śrī-ugracaṇḍāya namaḥ | Oṃ taptakāñcana... (and so forth).

Others [wear] earrings in the shape of coils and armlets; [they possess] jewel garlands and are endowed with power. [Holding] eighteen [attributes], they are beloved by the goddesses, nine-faced, and lotus-born. Likewise, [there is] the auspicious one holding a wheel, a vajra, and a goad, granting boons, holding a staff, and bearing a trident and a vessel.

Sobhitā: With her right hands [holding various implements], she is beautifully adorned with a bow, a mace, and a bell; holding a noose and a threatening gesture (tarjanī), she has six limbs and hair tied in a braid.
The mighty Daitya of great strength and prowess emerged;
his hair was known to be pierced by the trident.
Having meditated thus, the Great Goddess, of great splendor— [and so forth].
Khā, Khā, Hrīḥ, Sahastā, Khaṭvāṅgā, Ḍakarunā, Kṛṣṇā, Nīlā, Śuklā, Caturā,
Kaṃviṇā, Rudracaṇḍā, Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍogrā, and [the others] are the leaders.
Caṇḍā, Caṇḍavatī, Caṇḍarūpā, and Caṇḍikā;
Rocanā, Aruṇā, Kṛṣṇā, Nīlā, Śuklā, and Dhūmikā; Pītā, Pāṇḍarā, and Āgneyā; she who stands in the āliḍha posture and she who is seated upon a lion.
Accompanied by his own retinue, he comes here to this mandala.
[Thus ends the meditation; may there be auspiciousness.]

Oṃ! O God of gods, Mahādeva, you who bring benefit to the gods! Now I desire to hear about the Lord Muneśvara of Navadurga—his worship, meditation, fire-offering (homa), and what has been heard [regarding him].
O compassionate Maheśvara, I desire to hear all of this in its entirety.
The Lord said:
Listen, O Goddess Mahābhadrā, this is the most excellent of all mantras;
it must be recited with diligent effort, and not otherwise.
First, Rudracaṇḍā is said to be the Śakti Brahmāṇī.
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ rudracaṇḍā hūṃ brahmaṇī hrīṃ jvala hrīṃ svāhā.
She wears a crown of the eldest [deities] and is red in color.
She holds a conch, a bell, a skull-cup, a trident, and a khaṭvāṅga staff.
The Goddess, seated upon a buffalo throne, is surrounded by the bliss of Brahmā and the other gods;
having meditated thus, [one becomes] the great [Goddess] Śanī.
A triangle, a square, five [elements], and a four-petaled lotus with a pericarp.
One should worship Bhairava in the left triangle; in the [other] triangle, the protective goddess Brahmāṇī; and in the triangle, the supreme lotus. One should worship in the foremost triangle.
Suralocanī; Rudra is the deity of the staff.
Jayā, Vijayā, Ajitā, and Parājitā.
One should worship [the deity] within the supreme self, upon the auspicious petal of the lotus.
The dispeller of all obstacles.
Hereafter I shall speak: Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ jūṃ (2) pracaṭa (2) hūṃ (2) maheśvarī rakṣa (2) hrīṃ ehi (* * *?). This is called by the name Pracaṇḍā.

I shall proclaim [it], O you of excellent vows, concerning the one named Caṇḍogrā. As follows: Oṃ [caṇḍogrāya] grahastheśinā kaumārī [svāhā]. The goddess has eight arms, three eyes, and holds a conch, a discus, a skull-bowl, a trident, a raised index finger, a bow, an arrow, and a mace; she is the crusher of the demon Mahiṣāsura.
These two are the Great Goddesses who bestow all good fortune:
Jayā, the Great Goddess, is on the left, and Aparājitā is on the right;
O Lord of the Gods, Jayā is in front and Aparājitā is behind.
Just as one might conquer all the deities when they have been honored according to the rule. (3)
After this, I shall further describe the worship of Caṇḍanāyikā.
Oṃ Hrīṃ! She who is born and [who is] such-and-such, wearing two yellow garments in the forenoon;
O Goddess, she is mounted upon a bull and wears a crown of matted hair.
Having thus meditated upon the Great Goddess, who holds a trident, a hand-drum, a skull-topped staff, and a drinking vessel, she bestows the objects of one's desire.
The seasonal corner and the seasonal petal are square and triple-encircled;
in the seasonal corner, one should worship the Great Goddess, the daughter of the Ḍa-clan, and the others.

One should worship the Great Goddesses and the deities of the seasons upon the seasonal leaves with the syllables: rmryūṃ, śmryūṃ, lmryūṃ, kmryūṃ, smryūṃ, hmryūṃ. The summer vessel is to be worshipped, as are the vessels for the winter and the cool season, according to the following: rmryūṃ—O Great Goddess of the season! śmryūṃ—O Great Goddess of the season! lmryūṃ—O Great Goddess of the season! kmryūṃ—O Great Goddess of the season! smryūṃ—O Great Goddess of the season! hmryūṃ—O Great Goddess of the season! The summer vessel is to be worshipped, as are those for the winter and the cool season. As follows:
ŚLĀṂ TRAUṂ PLAUṂ HLAUṂ GLAUṂ MLAUṂ—O Great Goddess, one should worship the deities beginning with Indra and the rest in the square [mandala]; O Supreme Lady, she bestows the desired object.
Gāndhārī is on the left side, and Karālikā is on the right.

One should worship the Great Goddess Kālī at the front and Bhagamālinī at the back, O Supreme Lady, [for the sake of] all diseases (* * * *?). Hereafter, I shall describe those of fierce form and great power.
Oṃ hrīṃ kṣīṃ, burn, burn; strike, strike; shatter, shatter; O Indrāyanī, hūṃ! blaze, blaze! Dhūṃ! Svāhā!
Seated upon an elephant, he is blue in color and three-eyed;
he holds a vajra, a spear, a mace, a staff, a sword, a shield, and a bow.
Holding a mace, a goad, and a noose, as well as granting the gestures of fearlessness and boons,
[he wields] an arrow, the threatening finger, and a trident, with eyes blazing and flaming.

O Goddess, one should worship the charming Āge on the back, Caṇḍavatī likewise; Pralambhakā and others on the left, and the divine maidens on the right, O Supreme Lady, [she who] destroys all enemies.
Hereafter I shall proclaim Caṇḍikā Kālamocanī:
Oṃ śrīṃ jūṃ mṛtyuhare khphre cāmuṇḍike strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Mounted upon a corpse-seat: HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ VAISNAVĪ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
Seated upon Garuḍa, the Goddess has four arms and three eyes;
holding a conch, a discus, the gesture of fearlessness, and the boon-granting gesture, she is exceedingly gracious with a gentle smile.
Having meditated thus, the Great Goddess is the destroyer of timely death.
The great goddess Pūrvvarati is on the right, wearing yellow garments.
In the west is the goddess Vāruṇī, and in the north is Gadādharā.
Having worshipped the Great Goddess and paid obeisance according to the prescribed rite.
Hereafter, I shall proclaim Caṇḍāvatī, the sovereign goddess of the gods.
For example: Oṃ hrīṃ Caṇḍaroṣaṇī jvala (2) hrīṃ Vārāhī sa-sa-mahāghore hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
The Goddess beheld him mounted upon a buffalo, possessing ten arms and three eyes,
endowed with all ornaments, and adorned with human skulls.
The khaṭa, the kaṅkomuka, the khaṭvāṅga, the skull-cup, and likewise the boon-granting gesture;
as well as the plow, the pestle, the arrow, and the gesture of fearlessness.

And the Great Goddess Tarjanī, O Varāha, wherever she may be situated— in the fields, the secondary seats (upapīṭhas), and so forth— may those goddesses, who are worshipped by the lords of heroes (vīrendras) and are always pleased by the offering of incense, lamps, and the like, as well as by the rite of the auspicious bali-offering, protect you.

Pośi(? *? bhyas svāhā || Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ! To all the Yoginīs, to all beings, to those who dwell everywhere, to the inhabitants of the three worlds—accept this offering, worship, and oblation, svāhā! Śuklaṁ (? Śrī (?
Kṣūṁ Kṣeṁ Kṣīṁ Kṣa Hūṁ! To the Lords of the Fields (Kṣetrapālas) at the sacred sites, [this] incense, lamp, and meat.
"Accept the offering, svāhā! Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṃ, to Gaṇapati, [grant] the boon...
bring [the people] under control, svāhā! Having thus offered the fourfold oblation:

One should cause the recitation (*jāpa*) to be performed. Having recited the hymn of praise (*stotra*), one should offer prostrations again and again. With the words "May there be auspiciousness," [one concludes] the wheel of worship (*pūjācakra*). Having offered sandalwood paste with the root mantra, having offered flowers and unbroken rice (*akṣata*), [one offers] incense (*dhūpa*).
This essence produced from the lord of the forest, rich in fragrance, the most excellent scent,
a delight for all goddesses— may they accept it.
The mantra for the lamp.
Self-luminous, of great splendor, removing the three-fold impurities everywhere,
this lamp— the light that is both internal and external— be accepted.
Having offered with the root [mantra]...
The left hand is on the right side of the wheel; the front and the back; having then placed the vessel for the offering (balipātra) within a triangle.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vaṃ, obeisance to Vaṭukabhairava.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣaṃ, salutation to the guardians of the field (kṣetrapālas).
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, resplendent with a mass of tawny matted locks, three-eyed, with a flaming mouth, destroy all obstacles! (2) Together with [all the attendants], accept this offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Śrīṃ! Whether from the upper reaches of the Brahmāṇḍa, or in heaven, in the sky, on the surface of the earth,
or in the subterranean realm (pātāla), in the netherworld (nāla), or in the waters— [in whatever place]— [O Goddess],
[be present] in the first [element].
Kaṃ: I worship the sandals of Tripurasundarī, who pervades the reality of the Self, at the navel.
Haṃḥ! To the one who pervades the reality of knowledge (vidyātattva), [I offer] obeisance. In the heart.
Saṃḥ: I worship the sandals of Tripurasundarī, who pervades the Śiva-tattva. [On the head.]
Kaṃ Saṃ: I worship the sandals of Tripurasundarī, who pervades all principles (tattvas).
"In all limbs"—thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
One should visualize the *arghapātra* (offering vessel) as a triangle. Perform the worship with the six seats (*ṣaḍāsana*).

Within the triangle, one should worship Kāmeśvarī in the [eastern] corner, Vajreśvarī on the right, Bhagamālinī on the left, and Tripurasundarī in the center. One should worship her with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Thus concludes the worship of the *arghapātra*.

In the same manner, one should worship upon one's own head; having recited the root mantra three times, one should perform the fire offering (*homa*) in the tube-shaped hearth (*nāḍikuṇḍa*). Having prepared incense, lamps, and so forth, and having displayed the mudrās—this is the internal sacrifice (*antaryāga*) worship.
Then, at the gateway of the Jaga-maṇḍapa, Gaṇapati and Kṣetrapāla are to be worshipped with mantras on the right, left, and front [sides].
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the sandals of Matriśanātha.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, I worship the sandals of Oḍīśanātha.
Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, I worship the sandals of the one accompanied by Ṣaṣṭhī.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the sandals of Caryāśanātha.

One should worship [the deities] starting from Īśāna and ending with Āgneya. One should worship the six seats: the fourteen, the pair, the eight-cornered, the three-cornered, and the [remaining] two. Hsau, obeisance to the form of Mahātripurasundarī.
In the center is the form... the lotus... [and so forth].
[She] is like the *ruṇā* flower, resembling the *javākusuma*, and comparable to the *dāḍimī* flower.
With a complexion like a ruby and [anointed] with saffron,
she— [who was] (* * * * * * * * * * * * * * *?)— [beheld] her.
Her face, with its bud-like curved locks and the brilliance of her countenance,
bore a resemblance to the moon; it was like the soft fillet upon the forehead of the crooked [Lord Śiva].
The supreme goddess possesses a beautiful form shaped like the Pināka bow.
Her eyes were playfully swinging with waves of joy;
she wore shimmering golden earrings from which issued a mass of radiating rays;
her face was like a full orb of nectar that had conquered the moon.
Viśvakarman and others fashioned her, whose name was Suṣṭhuṣṭanāmikā, according to the sacred thread.
With lips as red as copper, coral, the bimba fruit, or water,
he who is like nectar has surpassed the ocean of sweetness by means of his smile.
Endowed with incomparable virtues, the great queen Kambugrīvā graced the region of her chin and possessed arms as lovely as lotus stalks.
Her lotus-like hands are as delicate as the petals of a blue lotus;
the radiance of the nails upon her lotus-hands has surpassed the surface of the sky.
She was adorned with a creeper-like necklace of pearls, possessed lofty breasts,
and her waist was beautifully graced with the three folds of skin.

Adorned with the cause [of beauty], she is like an eddy in the river of loveliness; O sinless one, she possesses a waist fashioned of jewels, a beautiful hip, and the line of hair upon her torso serves as an excellent goad for her thighs.
The mistress has thighs as delicate as a plantain tree;
she is adorned with a pair of shanks that are like a plantain tree of loveliness.
Her feet have firm ankles, and the soles of her feet are marked with the signs of the conch and lotus;
her lotus-feet are polished by the crest-jewels of Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
Resembling a hundred moons, with a radiance that causes a multitude of beauties to smile;
red like vermilion, resembling a heap of hibiscus flowers and pomegranates.
Clad in red garments, with noose, goad, and lotus raised [in her hands],
she has a red face, is smeared with red [unguents], and is adorned with red ornaments.
Four-armed, holding a bow and five arrows,
